_readme: Prices and request settings for option B. USD per million tokens. A model can make live or batch calls only when approved is true; edit approved yourself after checking the numbers against the provider's pricing page on the run date. A null price means unknown: dry-run then reports tokens only, and live calls are refused.

claude-sonnet-5-5.source: claude-api skill model table (cached 2026-11-03) and its prompt-caching notes: $2 / $10 per MTok, cache reads $0.10 (0.05x), cache writes 1.25x input for the 5-minute TTL and 2x for the 1-hour TTL, Message Batches 50% of standard. Not checked against the live pricing page.

request_settings.temperature: not set: non-default values are rejected on this model

notes: thinking: {type: disabled} returns a 400 on Claude Sonnet 5.5; {type: between_tools} is its way to turn thinking off, accepted only at effort high or below, with no other field.
No fallbacks parameter: the model string recorded with every answer must be the model that answered.
Structured output through output_config.format (json_schema); prefill is not allowed.

batch_limits.note: documented limit is 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch; the byte limit used here keeps a margin

gpt-5.4-2026-03-05.source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4 and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (platform.openai.com/docs/... redirects there), read 2026-11-24. Prices below are for prompts under 272K tokens (longer prompts are billed at 2x input and 1.5x output; ours are far shorter). Standard: input $2.50, cached input $0.25, output $15.00 per million tokens. Batch table row: input $1.25, output $7.50, cached input $0.13 (as listed). The pages were read through a web-fetch helper and quoted in part; re-check them before approving.

batch_limits.note: documented: up to 50,000 requests and a 200 MB input file per batch, one model per file, endpoint /v1/responses supported, completion window 24h only, up to 2,000 batches per hour; the byte limit used here keeps a 5% margin

notes: Model string: the dated snapshot gpt-5.4-2026-03-05, which the model page lists as the default snapshot of gpt-5.4 and the only one listed. It is sent in every request and recorded in every result file.
Reasoning effort: none (the model page: 'none (default), low, medium, high and xhigh'). It is sent explicitly and recorded in every result file.
Temperature: NOT set. Neither page says whether temperature is accepted at reasoning effort none; the Responses API reference lists it with a default of 1.

API: Responses API with text.format json_schema (strict: true; additionalProperties false; both fields required), no tools. The instructions go in a developer message at the start of input, because the prompt-caching page says to put reusable instructions there.

Cache-write fee: none listed for gpt-5.4. The pricing page's write-price columns are '-' for this model and the prompt-caching page says earlier models have 'No additional cache-write charge' (the 1.25x / 2.5x write rates it lists apply to GPT-5.6 and later). The page does not state outright that caching is free.

Cached input in batch: the batch table lists $0.13 for cached input (about half of $0.25). Whether prompt caching actually produces cache hits inside batch jobs is NOT documented on the batch or caching pages; estimates show a no-hit case beside the hit case.

Prompt caching is automatic. The 1,024-token minimum is stated for GPT-5.6 and later; for earlier models the page says the minimum 'varies by request settings' and gives no number. Our prompt is about 1,670 tokens (estimated). For earlier models cached_tokens is reported rounded down to a multiple of 128. Cached tokens are read from usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens and recorded for every call.

prompt_cache_key exists: it 'influences routing' and 'helps optimize cache routing on models before GPT-5.6'; it does not guarantee a hit, and the guidance is about 15 requests per minute per key. prompt_cache_keys: requests use keys verity-b-<prompt hash>-0 .. -(n-1), assigned round-robin in sorted pair order, each limited to --key-rpm requests per minute (default 12). Measured 2026-11-24: one fixed key cached 1,792 tokens once the shared prefix was about 1,870 tokens or longer (cache_diagnostic.txt).
prompt_cache_retention is not set (default). gpt-5.4 supports 'in_memory' and '24h'; no price difference was found, so 24h is not used without a reason.
store is false: responses are not stored.
output tokens include reasoning tokens (none expected at effort none); max_output_tokens is 64 (the API minimum is 16).
